s0446.literal: The Odes are what guide and express the mind and spirit, singing and chanting feelings and intent.
s0446.idiomatic: The Odes are what guide and express the mind and spirit, singing and chanting feelings and intent.

s0447.literal: Therefore it is said: "What is in the heart is intent; what is spoken forth is an ode."
s0447.idiomatic: Therefore it is said: "What is in the heart is intent; what is spoken forth is an ode."

s0448.literal: The ancients were pure and customs simple; feelings and intent were not yet confused.
s0448.idiomatic: The ancients were pure and customs simple; feelings and intent were not yet confused.

s0449.literal: Afterward the ruler was honored above and ministers were humble below; face-to-face praise was flattery and eye-to-eye remonstrance was slander, so chanting beauty and ridiculing evil served as satire.
s0449.idiomatic: Afterward the ruler was honored above and ministers were humble below; face-to-face praise was flattery and eye-to-eye remonstrance was slander, so chanting beauty and ridiculing evil served as satire.

s0450.literal: At first they only sang and chanted; later gentlemen set them to strings and pipes to preserve admonition.
s0450.idiomatic: At first they only sang and chanted; later gentlemen set them to strings and pipes to preserve admonition.

s0451.literal: Before Xia and Yin, most odes do not survive.
s0451.idiomatic: Before Xia and Yin, most odes do not survive.

s0452.literal: The Zhou house began with Hou Ji; Duke Liu solidified earlier achievements; Grand King laid the foundation of royal traces; King Wen glorified earlier accomplishments; King Wu conquered and pacified Yin's disorder; King Cheng and the Duke of Zhou transformed until Great Peace—they chanted beautiful virtue, following in succession.
s0452.idiomatic: The Zhou house began with Hou Ji; Duke Liu solidified earlier achievements; Grand King laid the foundation of royal traces; King Wen glorified earlier accomplishments; King Wu conquered and pacified Yin's disorder; King Cheng and the Duke of Zhou transformed until Great Peace—they chanted beautiful virtue, following in succession.

s0453.literal: Under You and Li there was turmoil and collapse; resentment and satire arose together.
s0453.idiomatic: Under You and Li there was turmoil and collapse; resentment and satire arose together.

s0454.literal: Afterward the king's beneficence was exhausted and the odes perished; Grand Master Zhi of Lu arranged and recorded them.
s0454.idiomatic: Afterward the king's beneficence was exhausted and the odes perished; Grand Master Zhi of Lu arranged and recorded them.

s0455.literal: Confucius edited the odes, taking from above the Shang and from below Lu—in all three hundred pieces.
s0455.idiomatic: Confucius edited the odes, taking from above the Shang and from below Lu—in all three hundred pieces.

s0456.literal: Down to Qin, they alone survived as material for recitation and were not destroyed.
s0456.idiomatic: Down to Qin, they alone survived as material for recitation and were not destroyed.

s0457.literal: At the beginning of Han, Shen Gong of Lu received the Odes from Fuqiu Bo and composed glosses—this was the Lu Odes.
s0457.idiomatic: At the beginning of Han, Shen Gong of Lu received the Odes from Fuqiu Bo and composed glosses—this was the Lu Odes.

s0458.literal: Yuan Gusheng of Qi also transmitted the Odes—this was the Qi Odes.
s0458.idiomatic: Yuan Gusheng of Qi also transmitted the Odes—this was the Qi Odes.

s0459.literal: Han Ying of Yan also transmitted the Odes—this was the Han Odes.
s0459.idiomatic: Han Ying of Yan also transmitted the Odes—this was the Han Odes.

s0460.literal: Down to Later Han, three schools were all established.
s0460.idiomatic: Down to Later Han, three schools were all established.

s0461.literal: At the beginning of Han, there was also Mao Chang of Zhao, skilled in the Odes, who claimed transmission from Zixia and composed a Gloss and Tradition—this was the old learning of the Mao Odes, but it was not established at court.
s0461.idiomatic: At the beginning of Han, there was also Mao Chang of Zhao, skilled in the Odes, who claimed transmission from Zixia and composed a Gloss and Tradition—this was the old learning of the Mao Odes, but it was not established at court.

s0462.literal: In Later Han there was Xie Manqing of Jiujiang, skilled in the Mao Odes, who also composed exegesis for it.
s0462.idiomatic: In Later Han there was Xie Manqing of Jiujiang, skilled in the Mao Odes, who also composed exegesis for it.

s0463.literal: Wei Jingzhong of Donghai received instruction from Manqing.
s0463.idiomatic: Wei Jingzhong of Donghai received instruction from Manqing.

s0464.literal: Earlier Confucians transmitted by succession called it the Mao Odes.
s0464.idiomatic: Earlier Confucians transmitted by succession called it the Mao Odes.

s0465.literal: The Preface was created by Zixia; Lord Mao and Jingzhong further refined and enriched it.
s0465.idiomatic: The Preface was created by Zixia; Lord Mao and Jingzhong further refined and enriched it.

s0466.literal: Zheng Zhong, Jia Kui, and Ma Rong all composed traditions of the Mao Odes; Zheng Xuan composed the Mao Odes Commentary.
s0466.idiomatic: Zheng Zhong, Jia Kui, and Ma Rong all composed traditions of the Mao Odes; Zheng Xuan composed the Mao Odes Commentary.

s0467.literal: The Qi Odes were already lost in Wei.
s0467.idiomatic: The Qi Odes were already lost in Wei.

s0468.literal: The Lu Odes perished in Western Jin.
s0468.idiomatic: The Lu Odes perished in Western Jin.

s0469.literal: Though the Han Odes survived, there was no one to transmit them.
s0469.idiomatic: Though the Han Odes survived, there was no one to transmit them.

s0470.literal: Only the Zheng Commentary on the Mao Odes stands alone to the present.
s0470.idiomatic: Only the Zheng Commentary on the Mao Odes stands alone to the present.
